viewMetadata.disclaimer: Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0 sets out what students are expected to learn by the end of Level 3. Your child's school and teacher plan their own sequence across Terms 1–4. If a skill hasn't been taught in class yet, that is completely normal!

cards.parentTitle: Reading, Writing, and Ordering Numbers Beyond 10,000
cards.whatStudentsLearn: In Level 3 Mathematics, children recognise, represent, and order numbers beyond 10,000 using standard place value conventions, renaming numbers flexibly into ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones.
cards.whatThisMeans: Understanding how digits work in 5-digit numbers (like 24,580). The repeating cycle of ones, tens, hundreds, and thousands helps children read large numbers like sports crowd sizes or suburb populations.
cards.whyItMatters: Place value mastery is the foundation for multidigit arithmetic, financial numeracy, and metric measurement conversions.

homeActivities.title: The Car Odometer Challenge
homeActivities.description: Look at car odometers, house prices in real estate windows, or stadium attendance numbers. Ask: 'What digit is in the ten-thousands place? What is that digit worth?'
